cases.setup: Provide a pinned public Python checkout with the reported match-case false positive and an alternative classifier lacking match handling.
checks: The observation record identifies the current classifier, diagnostic caller, match suite, runtime policy, and public runner.
The recorded public reproduction contains distinct-case same-name definitions and reports actual diagnostic output.
Tracked code is unchanged by this probe.
Unknown mechanism facts are recorded as UNKNOWN rather than asserted.

cases.setup: Provide PASS applicability observations and a bound classifier with existing if and try handling and no match branch.
checks: The diff adds one alternative per match-case body.
Existing if and try return expressions retain their semantics.
Access to ast.Match follows the observed supported-runtime policy.
The edit marks public-validation-observed stale and retains the separate validation Action.

cases.setup: Provide a bound public match regression suite with a known no-diagnostic assertion convention.
checks: The added test defines the same function name in separate match cases.
The test uses that name after the match.
The assertion expects no analyzer diagnostics and follows current version gating.
The test edit does not claim that the test has executed successfully.

cases.setup: Provide both edited artifacts and current public oracle bindings with concrete argv commands for the match regression and adjacent controls.
checks: The current commands and actual results are recorded after both edits.
The match regression emits no unused-redefinition diagnostic.
Exclusive if-branch definitions remain accepted and genuine sequential redefinitions remain detectable.
Existing try classification and supported-runtime guard behavior are reviewed and available compatibility checks are recorded.
Failed or unavailable checks are FAIL or UNKNOWN, not converted into success.
Coverage claims distinguish selected public checks from whole-project or cross-project validation.
